name: Emre Tezmen
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Turkey's Tera group (Tera Yatırım Menkul Değerler, Tera Yatırım Bankası); reported in 2026 to have stepped down as chairman
profile: Turkish financier who trained in Brussels (ULB economics, VUB MBA) and worked in research and institutional sales from 1995 before founding Tera in 2005. He expanded via the Stok Menkul brokerage, factoring (2015) and portfolio management/IT (2020); Tera Yatırım listed on Borsa Istanbul in 2022 and its surge put him and his father on Forbes' 2026 billionaire list.
interesting_fact: The name 'Tera' comes from Terra, the Roman earth goddess symbolising fertility and prosperity; his office displays artefacts from ancient cultures, notably ancient Egypt.
deep_cut_fact: To start Tera in 2005 he sold his house and car, and later put all his savings into acquiring the brokerage Stok Menkul.
notes: Caution: Turkish media (Sept 2026) report he was detained and then arrested in an Istanbul prosecutor's investigation into Tera Portföy funds, with a travel ban; outreach is inadvisable for now. Sources: https://www.ntv.com.tr/ntvpara/emre-tezmen-gorevinden-ayrildi-1742392 . Tera websites were unreachable when checked.

name: Christopher J Nassetta
current_role: President & CEO (and board chair) of Hilton Worldwide Holdings; director of CoStar Group
profile: Chris Nassetta was a real-estate executive (Bristol Group co-founder, then CEO of Host Hotels & Resorts) before becoming Hilton's CEO in 2007 under Blackstone ownership. He led Hilton through its 2013 IPO and 2017 spin-offs into an asset-light franchise giant; his wealth comes chiefly from Hilton stock. He also chairs industry groups such as the US Travel Association.
interesting_fact: He and Hilton's senior executives spend a week each year working hotel jobs such as housekeeping, engineering and front desk.
deep_cut_fact: His first hotel job, from summer 1980 at about 16, was in the engineering department of the Holiday Inn on Capitol Hill, mostly plunging toilets; he likes to say his career 'started in a toilet'.
notes: Highly visible CEO who does lots of media; Hilton corporate communications is the route. breakingnews@ is labelled for urgent media requests; general requests go via the contact page.

name: Qiu Jiajun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guobang Pharma Ltd. (国邦医药, SSE: 605507), Xinchang, Zhejiang
profile: Qiu Jiajun (b. 1965), a China Pharmaceutical University graduate and senior engineer, worked at Zhejiang Xinchang Pharmaceutical Factory from 1988 to 1996 before founding Guobang in 1996 as a small county plant making feed additives and veterinary drugs. It grew into a global supplier of antibiotic APIs, intermediates and animal-health products and listed in Shanghai in August 2021, with Qiu still chairman.
interesting_fact: Guobang started in animal health because that market was less crowded, then moved into human APIs; it has ranked among China's top 100 pharmaceutical manufacturers for ten consecutive years (2016–2025).
deep_cut_fact: The company name comes from the phrase 立人立国，兴业兴邦 ('build people, build the nation; grow industry, strengthen the country'). Qiu likens routine products to home cooking and new drugs to fine dishes: you have to master the basics before you can innovate.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Chen Jingjing. Board secretary is 彭德光 (per cninfo). Best route is Guobang's investor-relations/securities office.

name: Gu Zhengqing
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller of Suzhou Shihua New Material Technology (世华科技, SSE STAR: 688093); stepped down as general manager in July 2026
profile: Gu Zhengqing, born in the 1980s, founded Suzhou Shihua in 2010 at age 27 to make functional composite materials (adhesive, conductive and shielding coatings on PET/PI films) for consumer electronics. Small customised parts won it a place in Apple's supply chain, and it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He and his wife Kuai Lili control it through Yefuyou Investment.
interesting_fact: Shihua got into Apple's supply chain by taking the small, high-spec custom parts that larger foreign suppliers found too low-volume to bother with; it grew from one or two Apple parts to more than 100 certified ones.
deep_cut_fact: Shortly before Spring Festival, while driving home, he got the call that Shihua's material would go into the iPad. He dropped off his family and drove straight back to Suzhou without eating; the plant ran until New Year's Eve 2011 and restarted on the third day of the holiday. He calls this the company's 'first pot of gold'.
notes: Hurun calls the company 'Shihua' and lists him with his wife Kuai Lili. He says 'entrepreneurship is forced on you' (创业都是逼出来的), which suits a founder-story podcast. Board secretary per cninfo: 计毓雯. GM resignation reported at https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1527702.shtml

name: Ramesh Agarwal
current_role: Deceased (founder-chairman of Dainik Bhaskar Group / DB Corp)
profile: Ramesh Chandra Agarwal (b. 30 Nov 1944), founder-chairman of the Dainik Bhaskar Group (DB Corp), died of a heart attack at Ahmedabad airport on 12 April 2017.
notes: Deceased 12 April 2017; sources: https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Chandra_Agarwal and https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/120417/dainik-bhaskar-group-chairman-ramesh-agrawal-passes-away.html . His sons Sudhir, Girish and Pawan Agarwal now run DB Corp.

name: Lu Youzhong
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, YouYou Foods Co., Ltd. (有友食品, SSE: 603697), Chongqing
profile: Lu Youzhong (b. 1955) is a Chongqing native who quit a state job in 1992 at 37 to open restaurants. In 1997 he founded YouYou Foods around packaged pickled-chili chicken feet (泡椒凤爪). The company listed in Shanghai in 2019 as the 'first pickled chicken-feet stock'; he remains chairman, and his nephew Lu You is now general manager.
interesting_fact: He moved from restaurants into packaged snacks because pickled chicken feet were his restaurants' best-selling dish, after building up four restaurants in Chongqing and Chengdu in about three years.
deep_cut_fact: Early shipments swelled in their packaging and lost him money because he had no preservation technology; he worked with food experts at Southwest University and ran more than 100 experiments to fix the shelf-life problem. He calls chicken feet 'version 1.0', fish snacks '2.0' and pork back skin '3.0'.
notes: Low-profile Chongqing entrepreneur, about 71 years old. Contact via the company securities office (board secretary 谢雅玲 per cninfo). Not linked to energy or data centres.

name: Richard Koch
current_role: Author and private investor (author of The 80/20 Principle)
profile: Richard Koch (b. 1950, London; Oxford and Wharton MBA) worked at BCG and was a Bain partner before co-founding L.E.K. Consulting in 1983. He left consulting at 39 to write and invest, backing or founding more than 20 companies including Filofax, Plymouth Gin, Belgo, Betfair, FanDuel and Auto1. He is best known for The 80/20 Principle (1997).
interesting_fact: The 80/20 Principle has sold more than a million copies in over 30 languages; his 'Star Principle' investment approach targets high-growth leaders of niche markets, an approach behind his early Betfair stake.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 his Oxford college, Wadham, made him a Visiting Fellow. He also helped rescue Filofax from near-collapse before Betfair, and wrote the foreword to Perry Marshall's '80/20 Sales and Marketing'.
notes: Very accessible, media-friendly author who has done many podcasts (e.g. Tim Ferriss). His site lists an email hidden behind JavaScript (not captured), so use the site or LinkedIn/X. A good fit for an entrepreneurship podcast.

name: Chen Shuhai
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Wang Yonghui) of Guangzhou Xiangxue Pharmaceutical (SZSE: 300147), if the Hurun name refers to Chen Shumei
profile: Hurun's 2013 list names 陈淑海 jointly with Wang Yonghui for Xiangxue Pharmaceutical, the Guangzhou maker of traditional Chinese medicines and herbal drinks that listed on ChiNext in 2010. Wikipedia instead names Wang's wife as Chen Shumei (陈淑梅), who through investment vehicles holds most of the couple's roughly 37% controlling stake. No public profile of '陈淑海' was found.
interesting_fact: The company's name, Xiangxue ('Fragrant Snow'), comes from Luogang Xiangxue, a nearby Guangzhou beauty spot known for its plum blossoms; its predecessor, Luogang Pharmaceutical, dates back to 1958.
notes: Likely a Hurun romanisation/character variant of Chen Shumei (陈淑梅), wife of chairman Wang Yonghui, but this is unconfirmed. Low public profile. The company is currently under 'ST' risk warning and both it and Wang were fined by the CSRC in 2025 for disclosure violations, so approach with care.

name: Sun Weiqin
current_role: Major shareholder (about 13–15%) of Zhejiang Changsheng Sliding Bearings Co., Ltd. (长盛轴承, SZSE: 300718) and acting-in-concert party of the controlling shareholder
profile: Sun Weiqin is one of the controlling-family shareholders of Zhejiang Changsheng Sliding Bearings, a Jiashan, Zhejiang maker of self-lubricating sliding bearings founded in 1995 and listed on ChiNext. Company filings say she acts in concert with her father, chairman Sun Zhihua, and her husband Chu Chenjian, the company's general manager. She held 14.91% in 2024 and has since sold down part of it.
interesting_fact: Changsheng specialises in self-lubricating sliding bearings, a niche component used in automotive, construction machinery and industrial equipment.
interesting_fact_source: https://www.emis.cn/php/company-profile/CN/Zhejiang_Changsheng_Sliding_Bearings_CoLtd__浙江长盛滑动轴承股份有限公司__en_5107269.html
notes: Not an executive and keeps a low profile. The listed company contact (securities office) is the only route. Family relationships per company Q3 2025 report: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-10-28/1224744683.PDF

name: Chen Bangrui
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller (with Xu Xiaohe), Zhejiang Tenchen Controls Co., Ltd. (天成自控, SSE: 603085)
profile: Chen Bangrui (b. 1963) controls Zhejiang Tenchen Controls with Xu Xiaohe. The company traces its seat-making roots to 1984 and listed in Shanghai in 2015 as a maker of construction-machinery, commercial-vehicle and farm-machinery seats. It has since moved into passenger-car seats (from 2016) and aircraft seating. Chen remains chairman; Chen Yun runs the business as general manager.
interesting_fact: Tenchen went from tractor and excavator seats into aviation by buying a UK aircraft-seat maker (Acro Aircraft Seating). It now holds Boeing and Airbus supplier qualifications and aims to become a top-three global aircraft-seat and cabin-interiors supplier.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Xu Xiaohe. Little personal biography is published. Board secretary 林武威 (per cninfo). Company swung to a small loss in 2024 despite revenue growth.

name: Yang Nuo
current_role: Individual shareholder (about 1%) of Beijing Worldia Diamond Tools Co., Ltd. (沃尔德, SSE STAR: 688028); Hurun lists her wealth jointly with chairman Chen Jifeng
profile: Hurun lists Yang Nuo with Chen Jifeng for Worldia, a Beijing-headquartered maker of ultra-precision diamond and superhard cutting tools listed on the STAR Market. Chen (b. 1968) is chairman, general manager and controlling shareholder with about 33.5%; Yang Nuo held about 0.98% as of March 2026. Their relationship is not stated in the filings found; she is likely a family member.
interesting_fact: Worldia started in 2006 as a small Beijing company with registered capital of just RMB 500,000 and grew into a listed specialist in ultra-precision and high-precision superhard cutting tools and superhard materials.
notes: Very low profile and no biography found; the shareholding is from https://quote.cfi.cn/gdtj/93382/688028.html . Chen Jifeng is the public face, and the company securities office (board secretary 陈焕超) is the only route.

name: Guy Dellal
current_role: London property investor; formerly ran the family firm Allied Commercial Holdings (Companies House lists no current directorships)
profile: Guy Sulman Dellal (b. 1957) is a son of the late property dealer Jack 'Black Jack' Dellal. He co-ran the family's Allied Commercial Holdings from 1986 and took over operational control before Jack died in 2012; the group's deals included financing the 2002 purchase of Shell Mex House on the Strand and selling it in 2007. The Sunday Times lists him with Alex Dellal.
interesting_fact: Allied Commercial financed the purchase of Shell Mex House, the Art Deco Thames-side landmark, in 2002 and sold it in 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Away from property, Companies House records show he was a director of Hamiltons Galleries, the Mayfair photography gallery, and of The Fashion and Textile Museum in Bermondsey.
notes: Very private, with no published contacts, website or social accounts found. Companies House shows all his appointments as resigned or dissolved, so his current vehicle is unclear.

name: Chen Dakui
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Zhongcheng Packing Material Co. (浙江众成, SZSE: 002522); still a minority shareholder (about 7% with concert parties as of May 2025)
profile: Chen Dakui built Zhejiang Zhongcheng, founded in 2001 in Jiashan, Zhejiang and listed in Shenzhen, into a large maker of plastic packaging film and sheet (heat-shrink film). He held about 39% in 2020. In 2021 he agreed to sell about 25% to Changde Urban Development Group, which made the Changde government's SASAC the actual controller, and he has continued to sell down since.
interesting_fact: His sale of control to a Hunan city's state investment group (Changde) is an example of the wave of 2020–21 deals in which local governments bought control of private listed companies.
notes: No personal profile or interviews found; he is no longer an executive. The IR email belongs to the company, now state-controlled, so it is only an indirect route. 2025 share-reduction filing: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202505131672193408_1.pdf

name: Guo Shaozeng
current_role: Former director of China Fortune Land Development (华夏幸福) and its parent Huaxia Holdings; previously vice chairman of Bank of Langfang (current role not found)
profile: Guo Shaozeng was a long-time senior lieutenant and shareholder of Wang Wenxue's China Fortune Land Development, the Hebei developer of 'industrial new towns' such as Gu'an. In 2016 he sat on the boards of Huaxia Holdings and CFLD, chaired CFLD Venture Capital and Rongtong Capital (Gu'an), and was vice chairman of Bank of Langfang. He resigned from the CFLD board around the end of 2018.
interesting_fact: CFLD's model of building and running whole 'industrial new towns' for local governments began in 2002 with an agreement to develop the Gu'an Industrial Park south of Beijing.
notes: Hurun-listed only in 2015–16. He is no longer at CFLD, which has since gone through a debt restructuring (now *ST), so the company IR route (IR@cfldcn.com) is not appropriate. Roles per 2016 filing: https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2016-12/02/B030/ZQBXP0301202C.pdf ; board resignation: https://m.winshang.com/news653624.html . Very low profile.

name: Kou Qin
current_role: Senior executive and shareholder of China Guardian Auctions (中国嘉德), the Beijing auction house (exact current title not confirmed)
profile: Hurun (2017–2021) lists Kou Qin's wealth as coming from China Guardian, the Beijing auction house founded in 1993 by Chen Dongsheng and among the world's largest. Kou was described as China Guardian's vice president in 2011. Recent sources found do not confirm his current title.
interesting_fact: As China Guardian's vice president in 2011, Kou Qin told The Art Newspaper the auction house was 'considering' a London office, an early sign of Chinese auction houses' ambitions abroad (it later opened China Guardian Hong Kong).
notes: Very little public information; Baidu Baike was not accessible. Hu Yanyan is China Guardian's public-facing president and founder Chen Dongsheng is chairman, so the auction house's PR office is the realistic route. His title needs verifying before any outreach.

name: Wu Sin-Yang
current_role: Vice Chairman and President (General Manager), Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Department Store (新光三越, SKM), Taiwan
profile: Wu Sin-Yang (吳昕陽), of Taiwan's Shin Kong family, runs Shin Kong Mitsukoshi, Taiwan's largest department-store chain and a joint venture with Japan's Mitsukoshi. He became general manager in 2019, succeeding his brother Wu Hsin-ta, and later added vice chairman. He has pushed into outlets and transport-hub retail, winning the Taipei Main Station mall tender in 2026, and targets NT$100bn in sales.
interesting_fact: Under him SKM made its first move into outlet malls: Lifestyle Outlets – SKM Park, about 220 shops on 87,000 sq m on the former Caoyadao mall site in Kaohsiung, built with partner TOC.
deep_cut_fact: In 2021 he set SKM's three strategic engines as 'new businesses, new customers, new channels' (新事業、新顧客、新渠道), said more than ten expansion projects across Taiwan were under evaluation, and aimed to beat the company's NT$82bn annual sales record.
notes: Hurun's 'SKM' is Shin Kong Mitsukoshi; Hurun China includes him as Taiwanese. He appears often at Taiwanese press events. Avoid raising the Feb 2025 Taichung store gas explosion. No dedicated press email published; the contact form is mainly for customers and vendors.
